subject: [URGENT] Horizon AI — us-west-2 sustained latency & 500s; request for geo-drain
messages:
From: Horizon Ops <ops@horizon.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Support <support@horizon.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: sustained 99th pct latency and 500s in us-west-2

David / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sustained spike in 95/99th percentile latency starting ~07:40 PDT this morning across our us-west-2 footprint. Error rates for generation requests have climbed to ~8% (predominantly 502/504 for streaming endpoints) and throughput for our high-QPS service has dropped ~37% despite steady incoming traffic. We retried locally and are seeing KV cache miss amplification in traces.

This is impacting our SLAs (support queue is full). We need an urgent routing option: can you advise if a geo-drain or cross-region failover is possible for our production org? If so, what expected downtime and risk to session continuity?

Attached: sample request logs and a short trace (horizon_usw2_sample_logs.tar.gz).

--
Rachel Lee
SRE, Horizon AI
ops@horizon.ai
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Ops <ops@horizon.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sustained 99th pct latency and 500s in us-west-2

Team — taking lead. Summary: Horizon reporting 8% 5xx, 37% throughput drop in us-west-2; traces point to KV cache miss amplification and several worker nodes showing CPU stall/GC patterns.

Immediate asks:
- Stephanie: can you validate whether the us-west-2 kvcache eviction rate spiked across the cluster and if any instance OOMs/restarts coincided with 07:35–07:50?
- Hannah: coordinate an immediate cross-region routing pilot to us-west-1 for a small subset (10% of sessions) and confirm compatibility of pinned model variants. Can we do a staged drain without breaking active streaming sessions?
- Marissa: prep an exec note with ask for provisional credits / SLA exception if we need to force a geo-drain. Draft to include risk/impact bullet points.
- Priyom: pull top traces and logs, strip PII, attach to the ticket and link here.

I will loop in account lead after we validate the canary. Priority: get Horizon back to acceptable latency within the hour.

David
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Horizon Ops <ops@horizon.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sustained 99th pct latency and 500s in us-west-2

Quick update from runtime diagnostics:
- kvcache eviction rate jumped 18x between 07:33–07:41 in the Horizon tenant shard on us-west-2. Several workers reported >75% run-queue length and event-loop stalls. No OOMs recorded, but one node restarted its inference service at 07:39 due to a watchdog recovery.
- Kernel/kernel-selection path shows heavier fallback to slower kernels for long-context requests from the Horizon workload (their median context length spiked).
- We see localized NVLink contention on a subset of hosts (az3 rack).

Proposal (safe-to-execute):
1) Immediate: start a 10% canary shift of new sessions to us-west-1, keep existing streaming connections pinned for 30m to avoid partial output loss. This requires routing rule change + temporary model-variant fallback (same weights, lower dynamic batching).
2) If the canary reduces 99th pctl by >=30% for Horizon, escalate to a 50% shift.
3) Parallel: drain suspect AZ hosts in us-west-2 (az3) from the pool and mark for deeper host remediation.

Workload compatibility: model variants for Horizon are available in us-west-1 but we need to disable large-k cache prefetch for the canary (Stephanie will push config).

I'll execute 1) in 10 minutes pending go from Hannah on routing.

--
Stephanie
Director, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sustained 99th pct latency and 500s in us-west-2

Proceeding with canary now (09:05 PDT):
- Pushing routing rule: horizon-org -> 10% new sessions -> us-west-1.
- Applied model-variant fallback and disabled prefetch for canary sessions.
- Draining: isolate hosts in us-west-2 az3 from LB after current requests complete; keeping streaming sticky sessions intact for 30m.

Immediate observations (09:12 PDT): 99th pctl for canary sessions down ~42%, error-rate down to ~1.2% on that subset. Overall tenant latency is starting to trend down, customer-facing metrics will lag by ~2–3 minutes.

Marissa: David asked for an exec note. I’ve pasted a short bullet below for you to expand into a one-paragraph briefing for the account execs/CEO as needed.

- Issue: localized host resource starvation + kvcache eviction amplification in us-west-2 az3 causing throughput collapse and elevated 5xx.
- Action: staged canary to us-west-1 (10% new sessions) + isolate az3 hosts for remediation.
- Impact: immediate latency improvement on canary; rolling shift expected to stabilize SLA; short-term risk: streaming session continuity for long-context sessions if we do aggressive global drain.

Will keep updates every 15 minutes.

Hannah
Senior SRE, Regional Operations
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Horizon Ops <ops@horizon.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sustained 99th pct latency and 500s in us-west-2 — short update and next steps

Rachel / Horizon team — thank you for the rapid heads up and for sharing traces. Quick update from Redwood:

What we saw: localized host-level resource starvation and a KV-cache eviction amplification for the Horizon tenant shard in us-west-2 (az3). This created a feedback loop that increased tail latency and amplified retries, producing the elevated 5xx counts.

What we did: staging actions executed 09:05 PDT — a 10% canary of new sessions routed to us-west-1 with a model-variant fallback (disabled kvcache prefetch). Results: canary 99th pctl improved ~42% and canary error rate reduced to ~1.2%. We simultaneously isolated az3 hosts and have them in remediation.

Recommended next steps:
- If Horizon approves, we will increase routing to 50% new sessions to us-west-1 while preserving existing streaming sessions (expected stabilization window: 30–90 minutes).
- We will open a provisional SLA exception request while we perform host remediation; Marissa is preparing the text for your approval.
- Postmortem & long-term fix: runtime will implement a safer eviction/backpressure control and we will schedule a host-level hardware check for az3 rack.

Attachments: horizon_usw2_request_logs_08-16.tar.gz (stripped traces), kvcache_trace.html, proposed_sla_exception.pdf

We’ll hold on the 50% shift until we get your explicit go. Short call available if you want to review the plan — proposing 12:30 PDT.

Thanks,
David Kim
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
